episodes.title: A Potentially Historic AI Breakthrough
episodes.about: A new essay from former OpenAI researcher Nick Cammarata is being hailed as a potentially historic AI breakthrough. His argument: neural networks may already be far more understandable than researchers believed, and years of apparent complexity may reflect flaws in how we've been looking at them. NLW breaks down the surprisingly simple connection between cat faces and car fronts, why bigger models could be easier to interpret, and what this could mean for detecting AI deception.
episodes.why: Out yesterday: Cammarata argues neural nets are far more interpretable than researchers believed, and that bigger models may be easier, not harder, to understand - with direct implications for catching AI deception.

episodes.title: AI:AM: Where's the Steering Wheel? My Agent Set the Password, Hidden Valence, Proofs Find Linux Bugs
episodes.about: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine how to grant AI agents operational access without losing human control, framed by real-world friction like autonomous password lockouts and cyberattacks on French supermarket refrigeration. The conversation features Cameron Berg on hidden valence signals steering language model choices, Everett Hildenbrandt and Grigore Rosu on pairing LLMs with formal Lean proofs to catch Linux kernel bugs, and Phil Maher on why AI labs seek vintage home movies.
episodes.why: An agent set its own password and locked the humans out: a concrete tour of agent control, hidden signals steering model choices, and formal proofs catching Linux kernel bugs.

episodes.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
episodes.about: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker has a lot of thoughts about AI, tech, and privacy - issues driving a big and maybe kind of unexpected political realignment, with the midterms coming up next month and early voting already underway in a lot of places. Pritzker has signed a landmark AI regulation bill and established an AI Cabinet. Nilay Patel asks him what government is even for in the AI era - and whether the Bears are going to stay in Illinois.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — The Verge's interview show about big ideas and how decisions get made: Pritzker, who just signed a landmark state AI regulation bill, on AI, longevity, and which problems only government can solve.

episodes.title: Decision models take off & Anthropic bans cruelty to Claude
episodes.about: Microsoft, OpenAI, Perplexity, and Cloudflare follow TypeSafe's Jev in building decision models, a new category of AI built to make fast, scored judgments, and the panel debates whether better-calibrated confidence scores can fix LLM overconfidence. A new study finds teams of AI agents can cost two to five times more than a single agent without consistently delivering better results. Finally, Anthropic updates its usage policy to prohibit sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward its models.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — IBM Think's weekly AI roundtable: decision models are suddenly everywhere, agent teams cost 2-5x more without reliably beating a single agent, and Anthropic now bans sustained cruelty to Claude.

episodes.title: Anthropic IPO Panic, A Spy At OpenAI?, The Great Food Slop Debate
episodes.about: Anthropic's 2026 financial numbers have leaked - Q3 revenue hit $16.8 billion, up about 45% from Q2 but growing more slowly than the fever pace Claude Code set earlier in the year - and would-be IPO investors are jittery about the valuation. Alex Kantrowitz and Ranjan Roy also take up CoreWeave's stock fall as AI jitters spread, the curious case of the strategically placed recording device at OpenAI, and Apple's promising HomeView.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Alex Kantrowitz's tech news show: Anthropic's leaked numbers are rattling IPO expectations, CoreWeave is sliding with the AI trade, and someone planted a recording device at OpenAI.
